country_overview: Saudi Arabia operates a highly liberalised foreign-exchange regime administered by the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (SAMA). The Saudi Riyal is pegged to the US Dollar at a fixed rate of 3.75. There are no general exchange controls or restrictions on capital movement for residents or non-residents.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in or take out unlimited amounts of foreign currency and Saudi Riyal. No general currency declaration is required for normal travel amounts.
summary.business: Businesses and individuals enjoy full freedom to hold, transfer, convert and repatriate foreign currency through authorised banks and financial institutions.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Unlimited amounts of foreign currency and Saudi Riyal may be brought into Saudi Arabia with no general declaration requirement for travelers.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Unlimited amounts of foreign currency and Saudi Riyal may be taken out of Saudi Arabia with no general restriction or declaration requirement for travelers.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: No mandatory currency declaration threshold applies for ordinary travelers. Large or suspicious cash movements are subject to anti-money laundering reporting requirements by financial institutions.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Saudi residents may hold and maintain foreign currency accounts freely with authorised banks and financial institutions.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds freely without prior approval.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Business transactions may be invoiced and settled in foreign currency or SAR. Cross-border payments and repatriation of funds are handled freely through authorised financial institutions.
rules.exchange_controls: Saudi Arabia maintains no general exchange controls. The regime is fully liberalised for both current and capital account transactions.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion and transfers are widely available through banks, licensed money exchange houses, and ATMs throughout the Kingdom.
